reviewMethod: Independent visual sweep of all 32 paper pages and all Paper 2 scheme pages 22–47, with source cover. Every printed task cross-checked against the detailed mark allocation and required diagrams/context. Final crops inspected before publication.
sourceNotes: All ten questions retained: 46 tasks and 380 offered marks, despite 220 candidate marks. Q1(b) retains all three statistics together; Q7(a–b) shares 10C, and Q7(c)(i–ii) shares 5C.

Q1(a) accepts any suitable labelled chart. A labelled bar-chart example fills the scheme’s missing drawing. Q1(c) requires the third success on pick seven: exactly two successes among the first six, followed by a success, with replacement.
Q2(b) retains both scheme pages, including the complete Venn diagram and continuation of low/mid/high credit notes. All four probabilities are required, not a choice.
Q3(a)(i) is a statement for every real k, not a choice. Q3(a)(ii) slope formula excludes k=−1, where AP is vertical; Q3(a)(iii) gives k=−2.
Q4(b) asks for one horizontal and one vertical tangent, all under one 10C award. Any permissible pair is accepted; the four possible combinations are not separate cards.

Q5(b) requires all four angles between 0° and 720°. Q6(a) is one construction task. A clearly labelled NextStepUni construction supplies the missing diagram and construction lines; the official criteria follow unchanged.

Q7(a–b) retains the complete original scatterplot answer and correlation. Q7(c)(i–ii) gets an attributed worked line and estimate; reasonable by-eye lines remain acceptable. Full source table and graph accompany the question.

Q7(e)(i) uses the standard error 3.2/√12. Q7(e)(ii–iii) uses the first-season standard deviation as the scheme does; the two-tailed p-value is about 0.0078 using the scheme’s rounded z-score, or about 0.0079 at full precision. There is evidence of a change, not proof of the website’s claim.

Q8(a) asks to count groups, not choose a group. Q8(b) asks to count all codes; vowels and odd digits are data, not an option pool. Repeated digits are allowed. Q8(c) scheme prints 1.19 instead of 0.19 in the final product; its final €1.80 is correct.

Q8(d)(ii) the scheme uses the tabulated z=0.88 for cumulative probability 0.8093; the unrounded quantile is about 0.875 and the requested answer remains 73 g. Q8(d)(iii) conditions on large or extra-large, using 19/42, and includes both five and six extra-large eggs.
Q9(a)(iii) squares the map scale and converts cm² to km². Q9(c)(ii) compares relative errors using each possible true height as denominator; the largest is at 5.5°, giving 9.2%.
Q10(d)(iii) prints 5C beside three numeric bands 0,2,5; card uses 5B. Q10(d)(iv) prints 5D beside four bands 0,2,3,5; card uses 5C. No numeric awards changed.

Q10(d)(ii) is one congruence proof, not a choice of triangle combinations. Q10(d)(iv) offers two solution routes under one allocation; both retained. Its card includes the preceding requested results as context without supplying an answer.

cards.questionText: A farmer employs 14 workers to sort, pack, and load egg boxes for delivery. They work in groups of 5 at any one time. Find how many different groups of 5 workers it is possible to form.
